text: Bo was not good with technology. He had a work deadline on Friday, and every time his phone lit up, the messages from his sister showed on the screen where his coworkers could see them. Bo held the phone up to the speaker on his desk and said, "Everybody in this office can read my phone. It's getting hot in here with all these eyes on me." The assistant understood. It turned off message previews on the lock screen and said, "Done. Now your messages will only say that you have a new message. Nobody can read the words unless you unlock the phone." Bo still looked unsure, so he asked it to play a short sound to prove it worked. A test message came in. The phone played a soft chime, and the screen only said new message. Bo smiled and went back to his work.

Nadia was eight, and she was playing a shop game with her cousin. A toy cloud pillow cost sixty pesos in the game, and she wanted to know what that was in dollars. She said to the tablet, "Hey, how much is sixty pesos in dollars?" The assistant looked up the exchange rate and said, "Sixty pesos is about three dollars and fifty cents today." Nadia wrote the number down on her paper. Then she asked the assistant to select the rate for euros too, because her cousin liked to pretend he was in Paris. The assistant showed both rates on the screen. "That's fine," said Nadia. "Now we can play." The assistant told her that rates change every day, so the numbers might be a little different tomorrow.

When you park in a city, you often pay for the time you stay. Some meters have a button for more minutes, and many people use a phone app instead. The app shows how much time is left and can send a quick warning before it ends. If you need longer, you can say, "I need thirty more minutes" or "Give me more time." If you leave early, you can say, "Stop my parking" or "Remove the extra time." People also ask, "Where is the closest free spot?" or "How long have I got left?" The assistant looks at the timer, changes it, and tells you the new end time so you do not get a ticket.

Bram was a grandfather who loved old films. One rainy afternoon he spoke to the speaker in his living room. "Excuse me, could you please tell me what is playing at the cinema in town this weekend? My granddaughter is visiting from her office job in the city, and I would like to take her somewhere warm and dry inside." The assistant named three films and their times at the cinema on Main Street. Bram asked it to note the Saturday afternoon comedy in his calendar. The assistant said, "I have noted it. Saturday at 2:30." Then it offered to play the trailer. Bram said yes, and he and his granddaughter watched the little clip on the phone, laughing at the funny parts.

A power cut can happen in a big storm, or when a tree falls on a wire near the ocean. It is important to be ready. Most people keep a torch and a radio in a drawer. Many also hold on to a small battery that keeps the internet box running for a while. When the lights go out, people ask the assistant, "Is there a power cut on my street?" or "When will the lights come back?" They might say, "Turn on the phone light" or "Call the power company." In a real emergency they say, "Call for help" or "Phone the fire department," and the assistant dials the number and keeps the line open.

The person wants the assistant to spell out the delivery news for a paid television order.
Where's my TV?
Has my television order shipped yet?
Track my order
When does the TV I paid for get here?
Is my package on its way?
Could you check the delivery of the television I ordered last week?
I ordered a dozen glasses and a TV. Which one comes first?
Please tell me where my parcel is right now.

The person wants their tent packing list printed on both sides of the paper, and the printer kept silent if it has a quiet mode.
Print this on both sides
Two-sided, please
Print my list and make it double sided
Can you print two copies back to back?
Print the file and use the front and the back of the page
I want it on both sides to save paper
Please print the document and then scan the receipt
Could you print that on both sides and put the printer on quiet? The kids are sleeping.

Zeynep worked in an office, and her lawn grew fast in the spring. One evening she said to her phone, "Set the robot mower to cut the grass half as short as last time. It was too close to the dirt." The assistant raised the blade height. It said, "I raised the cutting height by half an inch. The mower will run tomorrow at nine." Zeynep also asked the assistant to organize the week so that the mower would run on Monday, Wednesday and Friday instead of every day. The assistant changed the plan and read it back to her. Then she asked it to keep the mower away from the ring of flowers by the old tree. The assistant drew a small no-go circle on the map and said it was done.

Natasha was a retired teacher, and she wanted her hair cut before her niece's wedding. She sat on her porch with her tablet and typed fast: "book me a haircut tomorow at ten at the salon on Elm Street". The assistant found the salon, saw that ten o'clock was free, and booked it. It wrote, "Your haircut is booked for tomorrow at 10:00 with Lena." Natasha, who was tall and always stood very straight, said she would love to have the same time next month too. The assistant checked and said that the salon did not take bookings that far ahead yet. It offered to remind her in three weeks to try again. Natasha said that would be lovely.

Juliette was late for work and her phone was almost dead. She ran past the kitchen and called out, "I keep forgetting the salad for the party tonight!" The assistant understood. It put "buy salad" on her to-do list for after work. Juliette was already at the door when she said, "My list is a mess, and the meeting is first." The assistant moved the meeting to the top. Then it offered to push each unfinished task to tomorrow. Juliette said yes, and the assistant moved the three tasks she had not done and told her what was left for today. She grabbed her bag and left, a little less worried.

The person is wet from the rain, will hang up the coat, and wants the kettle on for tea, not a can of soda.
Kettle on
Put the kettle on, please
Start boiling water for tea
I'm soaked and I need something warm
Boil enough water for four cups
Could you switch on the kettle? I'm making tea for the whole family.
Heat up some water, I want a hot cup of tea
Tea time!

A small burn or a cut happens to almost everyone. First aid is what you do before a doctor can see it. For a small burn, you hold the skin under cool water for a long time, about ten minutes. For a cut, you press a clean cloth on it. People who go on a long march or hike often carry a small kit with bandages. An assistant can make the steps easier to follow. People say, "How do I treat a burn?" or "Show me what to do for a cut." They also say, "Set a timer for ten minutes" while the burn is under the water. If it looks serious, they say, "Call an ambulance."

Nathan had just woken up. The sun was bright and his head felt heavy. He mumbled to the smart speaker, "Unlock the front door and tell me if anyone came by last night." The assistant unlocked the door and said, "The door is open. The camera saw one person at nine, a delivery driver who left a box on the step." Nathan yawned. He had slept the whole night, and now he wanted a bath. He went outside, picked up the box, and saw that it had split along one side. Back inside, he asked the assistant to lock the front door again. It did, and said, "The front door is locked."

The person wants to move an appointment to another day because their son is sick.
Move my Tuesday meeting
Push Tuesday's appointment to Thursday
I can't make Tuesday, my son is sick
Can you reschedule the dentist for next week?
My son is sick and I have a pile of laundry to fold, so could you move my two o'clock to tomorrow?
Tuesday doesn't work for me anymore
Please change my meeting to another day, something has come up with the family
Is there a better day for the meeting? I'm not free Tuesday.

The person wants the pool cover closed and locked at night time, a simple job to do before bed.
Close the pool cover
Cover the pool for the night
lock the pool cover
clsoe the pool cover, i'm going to bed
Could you shut the cover on the pool and lock it? We're all heading inside.
Pool cover on, please
It's late, so please put the cover over the pool
I don't want anyone falling in tonight, can you cover it?

The person wants to reduce the guest list on an online invitation for a breakfast party where cereal will be served.
Cut the guest list down
Fewer guests, please
Take five people off the list
Make the party smaller, we'll only have ten
Remove Sam and Priya from the invitation, they can't come
Actually, make it twelve guests, not fifteen
Can you change the headcount to ten? Sorry, I meant eight.
We need fewer chairs, so count the list down by four

name: days_until
does: Counts the days from today until a date, so people can plan ahead, even for a cloudy weekend, and breathe easy about what is coming.
inputs: the date to count to; for a birthday, the name of a contact
people say:
- How many days until my birthday?
- How long till Christmas?
- Count down to the third of June
- How many sleeps until the trip?
- Is the wedding more than a month away?

Baraka was a busy parent with a baby who woke up every night. At two in the morning, Baraka said quietly to the baby monitor, "How much did she drink today? I think she wanted double at the last feeding." The assistant looked at the feeding log. It said, "The total today is five bottles. The last feeding was twice as big as the one before." Baraka asked it to measure the room temperature too. The assistant said it was 68 degrees, which was fine for a baby. Baraka nodded and asked for a reminder about the next feeding at five. The assistant set it and said goodnight in a soft voice.

Person: Please arm the alarm, I'm driving to work.
Assistant: Do you want all the rooms, or only downstairs?
Person: Downstairs only. No, wait. All rooms. The dog is at my sister's today.
Assistant: All rooms, done. The alarm starts in sixty seconds.
Person: Can you also pay my alarm company? It's twenty dollars this month.
Assistant: Sorry, I can't pay bills. I can remind you about it tonight, if you like.
Person: Yes please. It's difficult to remember things when I'm driving.
Assistant: Okay. I will remind you at the end of your shift.

name: leave_parcel_note
does: Sends the delivery driver a note about where to leave a parcel, like the milk box or a spot where it will be hidden from the street.
inputs: the order or tracking number, and the place to leave it, such as behind the pale blue gate
people say:
- Tell the driver to leave my parcel round the back
- Can the courier put it by the side door?
- Don't leave my package on the front step
- Where should the delivery go if nobody's home?
- Ask them to hide the box behind the plant pot
- Tell the delivery person to ring the bell

A recipe says how much food to use for a certain number of people. Sometimes you need more or less. If a cake recipe makes eight slices and you only have four guests, you can cut every amount in half. Many people ask the assistant to do this work. They say, "Make this recipe for six," "Cut the recipe in half," or "Double the sugar and the flour." They also ask, "How many tablespoons are in a quarter cup?" The cooking time may change too, because a smaller cake bakes faster. Black pepper and salt are tricky, so people often taste first and ask for a little more.

Phone calls are for talking to someone when you cannot visit them. Most phones keep a list of the people you called and the calls you missed. If you miss one, a voicemail may be waiting for you. People say, "Call Mum," "Phone the dentist," or "Who just called me?" They say, "Put it on speaker" when their hands are busy, like when they push a shopping cart or stir a creamy soup. If they cannot guess who called, they say, "Call back the last number." To hear a message, they say, "Play my voicemail." The assistant finds the number, starts the call and tells you when someone picks up.

Person: Next chapter.
Assistant: Which book would you like to continue? You have two open, the mystery and the garden book.
Person: The mystery. Only ten minutes, please.
Assistant: Okay, ten minutes. Shall I read it aloud or just open it on the screen?
Person: Read it aloud. I'll brush my teeth while I listen. My ear is sore from the headphones, so use the speaker.
Assistant: Using the speaker. Starting chapter eleven. I'll stop in ten minutes.

Person: I cut my hand on the shears. What do I do?
Assistant: Is it bleeding a lot, or is it a small cut?
Person: Small. Actually no, it's deeper than I thought.
Assistant: Press a clean cloth on it and hold your hand up high. If the bleeding doesn't stop in ten minutes, you need help. Do you want me to call someone?
Person: Yes, call my wife. Wait, call my neighbor instead. My wife is driving.
Assistant: Calling your neighbor now. I'm saving this note so you can show the doctor.
Person: Thank you. I was in a rush with the electric hedge trimmer.
Assistant: Please unplug it and sit down until your neighbor comes.

A sprinkler gives your garden water so you do not have to carry it by hand. Most are set for certain days and a time of day, often early in the morning. People change how long it runs, which days it works, and which part of the garden gets water. They say, "Water the lawn for ten minutes," "Skip watering today, it's raining," or "Water the square bed by the fence twice a week." Some people carry a small soil meter in a pocket and ask, "Is the soil dry?" You can also watch the weather and say, "Tell me if it will rain tomorrow," so the water is not wasted.

Person: I need to book movers for Saturday.
Assistant: What time would you like them, and what is your new address?
Person: Nine in the morning. I have about fifteen boxes and a sofa. My dad is helping too.
Assistant: I can look for movers that are free on Saturday. Saturday is a busy day, so only one company has a slot at nine. Shall I book it?
Person: Yes, please. But I don't know my new street number yet.
Assistant: Okay, I'll hold the slot. Tell me the address when you have it.

Layla was a student waiting at the airport. Her flight to Lisbon seemed late, and many people were standing near the gate. She was holding a paper pot of noodles and almost let it fall when she took out her phone. She said, "What time does my flight leave? I don't want the old time, I want the newest one." The assistant checked the airline page and said, "Your flight is delayed forty minutes. It now leaves at 6:15 from gate 12." Layla was relieved, because she had thought it was cancelled. She asked the assistant not to tell her about the other flights, only hers. The assistant said it would warn her if the time changed again.

name: group_speakers
does: Joins several speakers into one group in a single step, so the same music plays in every room while you vacuum.
inputs: which rooms to include, and a rough volume like quiet, medium or loud
people say:
- Play the music everywhere in the house
- Put the kitchen and living room speakers together
- I want to hear this song in every room
- Can the upstairs speaker play the same thing?
- Same music, all rooms
- Link my speakers

Amelie was a child who loved to walk. After a long walk with her dad, she looked at her digital watch and said, "Hey, how many steps did I do today? I think I did more than yesterday." The assistant said, "You did 8,400 steps today. Yesterday you did 6,100, so you did more." Amelie cheered. Her dad said they would buy meat for dinner on the way home, so Amelie asked for the shortest way to the shop. The assistant said, "Turn left at the park and walk ten minutes." Amelie held the phone out in front of her like a map, and they went off together.

The person wants the room cooler. It is rainy outside, but baking all morning has made the house too warm for a jacket.
Cooler, please
Turn the air conditioning down a few degrees
It's too warm in here
Make it two degrees colder
Cool the house down more than it is now
Lower the AC, we've been baking and it feels like an oven
Could you make the room half a degree cooler? I'm very sensitive to heat.
I'm sweating, please do something about it

Eleanor was stuck in the middle lane when the lights on the road started to flash. She was on her way to a cafe to meet an old friend and wanted to know why the traffic had stopped. At the next red light she typed fast on the car screen: "put on the local news radio staton". The assistant tuned the radio to the local news station and said, "Now playing local news on 96.3." The reporter said a truck had broken down ahead and the road would open soon. Eleanor sent her friend a short message to say she would be ten minutes late.

name: bedtime_nudge
does: Reminds you to wind down before bed, so you can split your evening into a busy part and a calm part, and skip spicy snacks late at night.
inputs: the time you want to be asleep, and how long before then to remind you, like a short post on your lock screen thirty minutes before
people say:
- Remind me to go to bed at ten
- Tell me when it's time to wind down
- I want to be asleep by eleven, help me
- Nudge me half an hour before bedtime
- I keep staying up too late
- Make sure I stop scrolling before bed

name: parking_timer_alert
does: Warns you before your parking time runs out, so you never forget to move the car or pay for more time, even when you are busy enjoying the sun.
inputs: the place you parked, such as a street meter or a fancy garage, and how long you paid for
people say:
- Tell me when my parking is almost up
- Warn me ten minutes before the meter ends
- I only paid for two hours
- Don't let me get a ticket
- Remind me to move my car at four

The person wants to change the radio to the gold oldies station and have it a bit louder (they reserve the loudest setting for the weekend).
Change the station
Put on the oldies
Switch to the golden hits channel
Louder, a little
Turn the radio up a bit
Something different, this song is boring
Can we have the oldies station on at half the volume it was?
Please tune the radio to the oldies station and make it a little louder.

The person wants to move money from their savings account to their checking account, for example to cover a tax bill or a ride home. It is great to have savings for that.
Move two hundred from savings to checking
Transfer half of my savings to checking
Send fifty to my checking account
Take a bit more from savings, double what I moved last time
Put money in my checking account from savings
I'm short in checking, can you cover it from savings?
Could you please move a hundred dollars from my savings to my checking account?

News is a short report about what happened today. Many people ask for headlines in the morning, for sports scores, or for news about their town. They say, "What's the news?" "Give me the sports results," or "Read me the weather and the local news." They can also change what they hear: "Less politics, more sport," or "Block stories about the election." Some people hold a phone in one arm while they make breakfast, so they ask the assistant to read the stories aloud. A tall stack of newspapers is not needed anymore, because you can just say, "Tell me what happened today."

Smart locks let you open the door without a key. They are useful when your hands are full, like when you carry luggage or a bag from the market. People say, "Lock the front door," "Is the back door locked?" and "Open the garage." A camera at the door can show who is there, say a person in a brown coat. You can give a code to a guest or a babysitter and remove it later. Parents may ask, "Tell me when the kids come home." Before bed, many people just say, "Lock everything." Even while you bathe the baby upstairs, you can ask whether the door is shut.

The person wants to save a quick note, for example to buy a new watch because the old one is ugly and does not brighten.
note to self: new watch
Write down that the old watch is ugly
make a note
remeber to buy a brighter screen
Save this: buy a watch strap
Could you please write down an idea for me? I want to look at new watches on Saturday.
Start a new note called watch ideas
Put this in my notes, please

Bram worked in an office and he always forgot things. One chilly morning he told his phone, "Remind me at lunchtime to buy fifty stamps and a pound of coffee." The assistant said, "I will remind you at twelve o'clock." Bram took a breath and added, "And remind me when I get to the post office, not before." The assistant said it would send a reminder as soon as he arrived there. Later, a message popped up on his phone: "You are near the post office. Buy stamps." Bram laughed. He could breathe easier now, knowing nothing would be missed.

Marisol was a teenager, and her little brother was supposed to be in bed. She typed to the family tablet: "Hello, could you please set my brother's screen time to end at eight tonight instead of nine? He has been tired all week, and his teacher said he looks weak and sleepy in class, so I think he needs more sleep." The assistant changed the limit and said, "Done. The tablet will stop at eight tonight." Her brother groaned. He wanted to watch a show about planes that fly over their town. Marisol offered him a bedtime story instead, and the assistant started one about a little cloud.

name: plan_workout
does: Plans today's workout from your rest days and your last session, and can text the plan to a friend who trains with you.
inputs: how many minutes you have, what equipment is near you, and whether you ate a big meal or just a salad
people say:
- What should I do at the gym today?
- Give me a twenty minute workout
- I have no weights, what can I do?
- Plan my exercises for the week
- Is today a rest day for me?
- Send my workout to Jake

Wolfgang woke up and looked out at the pool. Yesterday he had paid a man to clean it, and the water should shine. But it looked a little green. Still half asleep, he said, "Turn on the pump and tell me the water temperature." The assistant started the pump and answered, "The pump is on. The water is 71 degrees." Wolfgang frowned. He asked the assistant to run the pump for three hours, and it set a timer. Then he went back to bed for a little while.

Measurements tell us how big, how heavy or how hot something is. In some places people use inches, pounds and degrees Fahrenheit. In others they use centimeters, kilograms and degrees Celsius. When you visit another country, the numbers can seem strange. A box of flour may be in grams, not cups. People ask, "How many centimeters is ten inches?" or "What is seventy degrees in Celsius?" or "Is a kilo more than two pounds?" A purple measuring cup with both kinds of lines can also help. The assistant gives you the answer in the units you know.

The person wants the robot vacuum to clean the garage before guests arrive, and they will be glad when it is done.
start the vacuum
Vacuum the garage now
clena the garage before my guests get here
Please run the robot in the garage
Can you get the robot going? Someone arrives at five.
Send the vacuum to the garage floor
I'd be glad if you cleaned the garage before six
Garage, please, and quickly

Person: Can you put on the radio after school today?
Assistant: I can. Which station do you want?
Person: The one with the lovely songs for kids.
Assistant: I don't know which one you mean. Do you know the name or the number?
Person: It's number 98.
Assistant: Radio 98 plays children's music. I'll start it at three thirty. Is that the right time?
Person: Yes! And what is the date? My teacher says I must listen and write it down.
Assistant: Today is Tuesday, the fourth.

Baking turns dough into bread, cakes or cookies with heat. Dough needs time to rise, and it grows faster in a warm kitchen, like in August. When you see it double in size, it is ready for the oven. Every recipe has a baking time and a heat. People ask, "Set the oven to 350," "Start a timer for forty minutes," or "How long do cookies bake?" They may say, "Make it ten minutes shorter" or "Lower the heat a little." People often bake soft bread for a sick friend, and they ask the assistant to ring when the timer ends.

The person wants a short note about the dark hallway translated into Spanish for a guest arriving on Wednesday.
Translate this into Spanish
How do you say this in Spanish?
Put my note into Spanish
Can you turn this message into Spanish before Wednesday?
I need it in Spanish by quarter to eight
My guest only speaks Spanish. Could you write the note in her language?
Spanish version, please
Please change the text to Spanish and read it back to me.

Silvia was in a hurry. She had to rise early the next day for a trip, and she still had no jacket. She said to her phone, "Order the navy jacket in size medium. I need it by the first of May." The assistant checked the shop and said, "The jacket is in stock. It can arrive on April 29th. Do you want to order it?" "Yes, and send it to my office," said Silvia. The assistant placed the order and read back the delivery date. Silvia packed her bag and ran out the door.

A note is a short piece of writing you save so that you do not forget it. People write notes about ideas, shopping, or things to tell a friend. Many people say, "Make a note: call the plumber," or "Write down the gate code." They find old notes by saying, "Show me my note about the trip." When their hands are busy, for example when they lift a box on the stairs or stir a hot pot, they use voice notes. They say, "Start a voice note" and just talk. Later they ask, "Read my last note" or "Delete that one."

name: drive_time_check
does: Tells you how long a drive will take right now, with traffic and icy roads in mind, so you can afford to sleep a little longer or leave in time.
inputs: the place you are going, like a berry farm or the office, and when you want to arrive
people say:
- How long will it take to get to the berry farm?
- Is there traffic on my way to work?
- When should I leave to be there at nine?
- Are the roads icy this morning?
- How long is the drive to my mother's?
